General

A dim helps focus user attention on a specific overlay component by reducing the visibility of the background interface.

When to use

Use a dim for overlay components such as a modal dialog, notification or menu.

When not to use

Avoid using a dim when maintaining visibility of the background interface is essential for user context or when it may hinder user interactions with other elements on the interface.


Use Directives

Size

The dim asset is currently set to a fixed width and height, the user must manually change this to take uo the whole size of screen that they are designing on.

Placement

The dim component always has to fill the entire screen.


Component Variants

Single dim component variation

There is only one dim component variation, as it is uop to the user to manually set the height and width.

Examples


Accessibility

This OneDS component is compliant with WCAG 2.2 AA Standards.

Design considerations

Dim should block the interaction with background content while the modal is open. Tab should never land on the dim.
The screenreader should not announce the dim at all. Dim should prevent screen reader navigation to content outside the modal.
Focus should be trapped inside the modal content.
The Dim itself does not require a specific contrast ratio, because it is not a focusable or readable element.
Development considerations

No further development considerations required.

While this individual component is accessible, building fully usable interfaces requires further attention. For guidance, refer to our OneExperience OneExperience accessibility resources.
